image:
  repository: forge.ko.ag/sauyon/lemonade
  # Bump on each rebuild. CI tags as :sha-<short> alongside :latest;
  # pinning to a sha keeps ArgoCD diffs explicit.
  tag: "sha-e785204"
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  # No pullSecrets: package visibility follows the owner, and `sauyon` is a
  # public user, so the kubelet pulls this anonymously.

replicas: 1

# Models that the init wrapper registers + loads at first start. The /v1/pull
# calls are idempotent against the PVC's user_models.json, so restarts skip
# downloads. Backend options are pinned via /v1/load with save_options=true,
# persisting to ~/.cache/lemonade/recipe_options.json.
models:
  # `user.*` namespace required by Lemonade for HF-registered models.
  #
  # huihui-ai abliterated build of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (refusal-direction
  # removed via Arditi et al.). Quant tag is repo-native plain Q4_K — this
  # repo ships Q2_K..Q8_0 with no _M/_S split. Despite the "MTP-GGUF" repo
  # name, the only extra file is mmproj-model-f16.gguf (VLM projector);
  # there is no MTP draft file like ggml-org/* ships, so the resolver
  # won't accidentally pick a draft GGUF as the main model.
  #
  # Name is ALL-LOWERCASE on purpose. Lemonade matches model ids
  # case-sensitively, but Cloudflare AI Gateway lowercases the model field
  # before forwarding to a custom provider. A mixed-case name therefore
  # 404s (→ 502) for every request that arrives via ai.ko.ag/CF AIG, while
  # working fine on direct in-cluster calls. Keeping the registered id
  # lowercase makes CF's normalization a no-op. See docs/lemonade-cf-aig-model-casing.md.
  - name: "user.qwen3.6-35b-abliterated"
    checkpoint: "huihui-ai/Huihui-Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-abliterated-MTP-GGUF:Q4_K"
    # Vulkan wins on Strix Halo across the board in our bench; ROCm
    # variance was poor on MoE long-context (+/-11 t/s on 17.95).
    backend: "vulkan"
    # Total context across all slots -- llama.cpp's `--ctx-size` is total, not
    # per-slot. llama-server then caps each slot at the model's training
    # context, 262144 here, logging "the slot context (N) exceeds the training
    # context of the model". So the only ctxSize worth setting is
    # parallelSlots * 262144; anything above that is allocated and wasted, and
    # anything below shortens every slot for no gain.
    #
    # Four slots because every observed failure was a fan-out of 3+ concurrent
    # requests queueing against 2 slots until the client gave up. Costs ~4Gi of
    # the 96Gi Vulkan/GTT budget over two slots (24.5Gi -> 28.6Gi measured);
    # GTT is charged to host DRAM but never to this pod's cgroup, so the memory
    # limit below does not move. See docs/lemonade-prompt-cache.md.
    ctxSize: 1048576
    parallelSlots: 4
    # KV cache quant. Q4_0 halves Q8_0 again, which is required to fit
    # long-context slots under the pod limit. If Vulkan fails to load with
    # a cache type support error, fall back to q8_0 and drop slots.
    kvCacheType: "q4_0"
    # Required for non-f16 KV quant to actually save memory at runtime.
    flashAttention: true
    # Overrides the template baked into the GGUF, which rejects any system
    # message that is not first. Clients that send two — opencode does, once
    # a memory plugin is loaded — get a 400 on every request without this.
    # Names a file under files/. See docs/lemonade-chat-template.md.
    chatTemplateFile: "qwen3.6-sysmerge.jinja"
    # llama-server's `--cache-ram`: the RAM ceiling for saved prompt state,
    # which is what lets a conversation resume without re-evaluating its whole
    # prompt. Default 8192 evicted 3 times in 48h. This cgroup has swap
    # disabled, so every MiB here is permanently resident.
    cacheRamMiB: 16384
    # llama-server's `--ctx-checkpoints`. Each checkpoint is a flat 62.8 MiB,
    # so the default 32 lets one long conversation hold ~2 GiB of the cache
    # above. Restores here land on the newest checkpoint, so the deep history
    # bought nothing. See docs/lemonade-prompt-cache.md.
    ctxCheckpoints: 8

# Sole registered model, so this is also what clients that do not pass a
# model explicitly get.
defaultModel: "user.qwen3.6-35b-abliterated"

# Make `models:` above authoritative: on every start, drop registry entries
# on the PVC that aren't listed there. Without this, registrations are
# add-only and survive forever — a model removed from this file keeps
# showing up in /api/tags, which is how the mixed-case Qwen orphan outlived
# the rename. Set false if you want to register models by hand through
# lemond's web UI and have them stick across restarts.
#
# Prunes registrations only, never GGUF blobs — see the entrypoint comment
# in templates/configmap.yaml for why that split is deliberate.
pruneUnmanagedModels: true

# Lemonade caches HF downloads + recipe_options.json under /root/.cache.
# 100 GiB is oversized now that Qwen3.6 35B-A3B Q4_K (~21 GiB) is the only

# capacity gate by hostPath-mounting the render node directly; pod

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 709661 | 22:43:54 | 22:47:21 | 3m27s | 1665 |

| 709024 | 22:41:26 | 22:48:08 | 6m42s | 7000 |

`n_tokens` there is total slot context (prompt + generated). Cross-referencing `n_decoded` at 22:45:50 (1988 / 1442 / 260), the generated portions land around 2000, 1500, and 400 tokens. That's ordinary reasoning-model output for a mail-triage prompt. Nothing ran away, and every slot released cleanly.

What I did wrong: I saw `n_decoded` crawling up by 1 token per log line and the `tg` average sliding (8.93 → 7.88) and read "stuck." Those are the same observation as contention, and I picked the more dramatic reading. I also latched onto `reasoning-budget: activated, budget=2147483647` as corroboration — that's just the no-cap default, not evidence of anything. It shouldn't have moved my conclusion.

What survives: all 4 slots were genuinely occupied, litellm caps at `max_parallel_requests: 4`, so my test queued. Real cause of the wait is that Qwen-3.6-35B under 4-way concurrency does ~2–8 t/s per slot, so a 2000-token answer takes minutes — and hakobiya was holding slots with multi-minute triage requests back to back. Slow and busy, not broken and not stuck.

That also means the "10-minute hang" framing I gave you was wrong: I'd have gotten an answer if I'd waited, since litellm's 600s lemonade timeout is per-chunk, not total.

Still open from before: I never reproduced whatever *you* saw. Qwen answers fine now (1.4s, 31 t/s idle). What was the actual symptom?
opencode doesn't handle contention well at all

Root cause found, with evidence. Your read was right — it's contention, and opencode's transport dies on it.

**Only one live error class.** Everything else stopped on or before 2026-08-15:

| error | total | today |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream returned 524` | 180 | **56** |
| `litellm ... No fallback model group found` | 422 | 0 (fixed 08-15) |
| `AI_APICallError: <none>` | 76 | 0 |
| `Server returned nothing` / `Bad Gateway` / `500` | 77 | 0 |

All 56 of today's 524s fall in a single hour — 22:00Z — the exact window hakobiya had lemonade's slots pinned. By agent: `plan` 32, `undefined` 20, `memory-recall` 14, `title` 4.

**The chain:**
1. lemonade has 4 slots; litellm caps at `max_parallel_requests: 4`. Under load your request queues.
2. While queued *and* during prefill, litellm emits zero bytes. Its lemonade deployment carries `timeout: 600`, so litellm itself will happily wait 10 minutes.
3. But the **CF AI Gateway → `ai-origin.ko.ag` tunnel** leg gives up around 100s and returns 524.
4. Your worker had already passed `HEADER_RACE_MS` (20s), committed to a 200, and started keepalive pings — so it can no longer send a status. It reports the failure in-band via `writeErrorEvent` (`workers/ai-gateway/index.js:96`), which is literally where the string `upstream returned 524` comes from.
5. opencode sees that mid-stream and logs `stream error`.

**The gap:** the worker's keepalive protects client↔worker. Nothing protects worker↔AIG↔origin. Your own comment at `index.js:15-30` anticipated the client leg but not the inner one.

**Not the cause:** opencode's timeouts. I checked the 1.18.3 binary — `timeout`/`headerTimeout`/`chunkTimeout` all default to unset for a custom provider; only the built-in `openai` integration injects a `headerTimeout`. Left alone, opencode waits indefinitely. It's the transport that hard-fails, not the client.

**Recommendation, given you want Qwen and not GLM:** cut AI Gateway out of the path — have the worker dial `ai-origin.ko.ag` directly. That deletes the unprotected leg, and the existing keepalive then covers the whole request, so a queued Qwen call just waits instead of dying. Cost is AIG's logging/caching/rate-limiting.

The cheaper one-liner — dropping litellm's lemonade `timeout: 600` to ~90s so it fails over before AIG bites — I'd skip: it "works" by handing you GLM, which is the thing you told me you don't want.

# Reaching litellm (and why Cloudflare is no longer in front of it)

litellm is the OpenAI-compatible router in front of the local model: it serves
`glm` and fails over lemonade → Z.ai Coding Plan → OpenRouter
(`charts/litellm/values.yaml`).

**It has no public endpoint.** The Cloudflare path was deleted on 2026-08-26.

## How to reach it

| Caller | Address | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| In-cluster pod | `http://litellm.litellm.svc.cluster.local:4000/v1` | The normal case. Callers must be in a namespace listed in `networkPolicy.allowFrom`. |
| A cluster **node** (fujiwara, meiko, mio, yui) | `http://10.43.64.156:4000/v1` | Pinned ClusterIP. A node's host netns cannot resolve `cluster.local`, so the address is the interface — same reason `charts/ssh-oidc` pins one. |
| Port-scanning clients (odysseus) | `:11434` on the same Service | `service.compatPort`, an ollama-style second front door onto the same `targetPort`. |
| LAN host, or a laptop on the `10.9.0.0/24` WireGuard VPN | `http://10.0.7.240:4000/v1` | Cilium LoadBalancer address, L2-announced. **Requires `Authorization: Bearer <master key>`** — unlike the two rows above, which are unauthenticated by network position. |

**litellm now runs with a master key** (`general_settings.master_key`, from the
`litellm-master-key` Secret). In-cluster and on-node callers still reach it
without one only because the NetworkPolicy admits them by namespace; anything
arriving at the LoadBalancer address must present it.

The key must exist in three namespaces under three different key names —
`litellm/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY`, `hakobiya/OPENAI_API_KEY`, `opencode/apiKey`. The
one command that creates all three is in `charts/litellm/values.yaml`.

## Why the Cloudflare path had to go: an unfixable 524

The old path made two edge traversals to reach a service in this cluster:

```
client → ai.ko.ag                (Workers script, custom domain)
       → gateway.ai.cloudflare.com   (CF AI Gateway, custom-ollama provider)
       → ai-origin.ko.ag             (back through the CF edge)
       → cloudflared tunnel → litellm.litellm.svc:4000
```

The mechanism that killed it:

1. **litellm emits nothing until its upstream produces a first token.** Measured
   at 600s of complete silence on a large prompt. lemonade did not have this
   problem — it flushes headers in ~0.5ms and then goes quiet — so the failure
   only appeared when the origin behind `ai.ko.ag` became litellm.
2. **Cloudflare reads a silent origin as a dead one and returns 524.** Observed
   at 255s; a 110s request survived, so the cutoff sits between. The ceiling is
   not configurable below Enterprise (`docs/gateway-timeouts.md`).
3. **The Worker's SSE keepalive only ever covered one of the two hops.** It
   emitted `: keepalive` comment lines toward the client once a request passed a
   20s header race — but only for `stream: true`, since comments would corrupt a
   JSON body. Non-streaming requests were never covered.
4. **The inner hop could not be covered at all.** Between CF AI Gateway and
   `ai-origin.ko.ag` the silent party *is* the origin, so there is nobody in a
   position to send a keepalive. No amount of Worker code reaches that hop.

So the 524s were structural, not a tuning problem. The evidence at teardown time
was a cloudflared log full of `Incoming request ended abruptly: context
canceled` against `ai-origin.ko.ag/v1/chat/completions`.

**Re-homing onto an `*.ko.ag` HTTPRoute would have been worse, not better** —
that path is capped at ~100s by the same edge, versus the ~255s the AI Gateway
path tolerated. Every Cloudflare-fronted option loses to a cold prompt eval.

**The same silence bites in-cluster callers too**, for a different reason and
with a different fix: a litellm rollout leaves its Service with no ready
endpoint for minutes, and a caller with no deadline hangs rather than failing
over. That is `docs/litellm-rollout-blast-radius.md`, and its advice — give every
consumer a finite read deadline — still stands. Removing the public path did not
change it, because those consumers reach litellm in-cluster and their *own*
public hostnames are still Cloudflare-fronted with the same ~100s budget.

## What was deleted

- `workers/ai-gateway/` — the entire Workers façade.
- `cloudflare_workers_script.ai_gateway_facade` + `cloudflare_workers_custom_domain.ai_gateway`.
- Both Access apps and policies: the `ai.ko.ag` all-IPs bypass, and the
  `ai-origin.ko.ag` Cloudflare-IPs-only `non_identity` policy (plus the
  `data.cloudflare_ip_ranges` it consumed).
- `null_resource.ai_gateway_custom_provider_base_url` — the REST PATCH that kept
  the `custom-ollama` provider's `base_url` pointed at the origin hostname.
- The `ai-origin` tunnel ingress rule and its proxied CNAME in `tf/argocd.tf`.
